To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

niosome is an appropriate drug delivery system for SGR, the effect of salt and temperature on the encapsulated drug is significant and the disruption of niosomes by cyclodextrin is a useful technique to study the effect of CD on cell membrane.
the niosome-bound drug is more stable in the presence of salts as well as in the higher temperature, whereas CDs are found to be more disruptive to niosome than to the cell membrane.
the photophysical properties and the drug encapsulation efficiency of niosomes are highly sensitive toward the environmental changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the photophysics of SGR encapsulated in niosomes and the effect of CDs in the drug sequestration process.
the study of the photophysical properties and the encapsulation of a bioactive drug in the niosome.
the investigation of niosome as a drug delivery system and its interaction with the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the drug sequestration from niosome is possible by CDs, but it is a slow process.

the encapsulation of the drug inside niosome is highly advantageous for the delivery purpose as it provides a microheterogeneous milieu for the drug which is capable of stabilizing the drug in a particular form and can be easily disrupted by the CDs.
the niosome is a suitable vehicle for the encapsulation of SGR, which can be used for the treatment of cancerous diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the niosomal formulation is a potential carrier system for the anticancer drug, SGR.
the drug sequestration inside the niosome is highly dependent on the environmental conditions and can be disrupted by CDs.
the encapsulation of bio-active drug into niosome is a feasible approach for drug delivery system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the drug sequestration from niosome is not a simple phenomenon.
the niosome-bound anticancer drug is stabilized by the presence of salts and temperature.
the encapsulation of SGR in niosome is found to be a better approach to protect the drug molecule from the deleterious effects of salts and temperature.
